# Disagreement Log — 2 Maccabees Chapter 14
**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 20

---

## V.3 — "times of separation" vs. "time of the mingling" vs. "period of forced assimilation"
- EMET: "times of separation" (inverts the Greek)
- LOGOS: "time of the mingling with the Gentiles" (literal *kraseis*)
- PNEUMA: "period of forced assimilation" (interpretive)
- SOPHIA: LOGOS — Greek *kraseis*: minglings/mixing; the reference is to Antiochus's hellenization program

## V.3 — "willfully defiled himself" vs. "deliberately defiled himself" vs. "deliberately defiled himself"
- EMET: "willfully"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "deliberately"
- SOPHIA: "deliberately" — *hekōn*: voluntarily/deliberately; LOGOS preferred

## V.4 — "brought him a crown of gold" vs. "bringing him a golden crown" vs. "bringing a gold crown"
- Minor variation — all essentially agree
- SOPHIA: "a golden crown" — LOGOS phrasing

## V.6 — "keeping up war" vs. "maintaining a state of war" vs. "waging constant war"
- EMET: "keeping up war"
- LOGOS: "maintaining a state of war"
- PNEUMA: "waging constant war" (adds "constant" not in Greek)
- SOPHIA: LOGOS phrasing

## V.7 — "ancestral glory" vs. "ancestral dignity" vs. "honor of my ancestors"
- EMET: "glory" (*doxan*)
- LOGOS: "dignity"
- PNEUMA: "honor"
- SOPHIA: "ancestral honor" — Greek *tēn patrikēn doxan*: ancestral glory/honor; EMET's "glory" is defensible but "honor" better captures the priestly dignity context

## V.15 — "comes to the aid of his inheritance by manifestation" vs. "upholds his inheritance with his appearing" vs. "defends his inheritance with his appearing"
- EMET: "by manifestation"
- LOGOS: "with his appearing"
- PNEUMA: "with his appearing"
- SOPHIA: "by his appearing" — Greek *tē epiphaneia*: by the appearing/manifestation; the *epiphania* language is central to this book's theology

## V.18 — "was afraid to decide the matter by bloodshed" vs. "shrank from settling the matter by bloodshed" vs. "held back from forcing a bloodbath"
- EMET: "was afraid to decide"
- LOGOS: "shrank from settling"
- PNEUMA: "held back from forcing a bloodbath"
- SOPHIA: "was reluctant to settle the matter by bloodshed" — synthesis of EMET/LOGOS

## V.25 — "shared in the common life" vs. "shared in the common lot of men" vs. "enjoyed the common pleasures of living"
- EMET: "common life"
- LOGOS: "common lot of men"
- PNEUMA: "common pleasures of living" (adds "pleasures")
- SOPHIA: "common lot" — Greek *bion koinon*: common life/lot; LOGOS preferred

## V.30 — "more austerely" vs. "growing colder" vs. "growing distant, more abrupt"
- EMET: "more austerely"
- LOGOS: "growing colder"
- PNEUMA: "growing distant, more abrupt" (expands significantly)
- SOPHIA: "growing colder" — LOGOS; captures the relational cooling

## V.33 — "level this sanctuary to the ground" vs. "raze this shrine of God to the ground" vs. "tear this shrine of God to the ground"
- EMET: "level"
- LOGOS: "raze"
- PNEUMA: "tear"
- SOPHIA: "raze" — LOGOS; standard term for demolishing a sacred building

## V.33 — "a splendid temple to Dionysus" vs. "a magnificent temple to Dionysus" vs. "a magnificent temple to Dionysus"
- EMET: "splendid"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "magnificent"
- SOPHIA: "magnificent" — Greek *episēmon*: notable/magnificent

## V.38 — "times of separation" vs. "earlier times of separation" vs. "earlier days, when there was no forced mixing"
- Note: EMET and LOGOS differ on the Greek *kraseis* (mingling) vs. its absence
- SOPHIA: LOGOS — "in the former times, when there was no intermingling"

## V.38 — "submitted his body and soul in full earnestness" vs. "devoted body and soul with complete earnestness" vs. "offered up body and soul with total dedication"
- EMET: "submitted"
- LOGOS: "devoted"
- PNEUMA: "offered up"
- SOPHIA: "committed body and soul with complete earnestness" — Greek *parabaloumenos*: risking/staking; "committed" captures both devotion and risk

## V.41 — "having drawn his sword" vs. "fell upon his own sword" vs. "drew his sword"
- EMET: "having drawn his sword" (does not clearly say he fell on it)
- LOGOS: "fell upon his own sword" (clarifies the action)
- PNEUMA: "drew his sword"
- SOPHIA: LOGOS — "fell upon his own sword"; the Greek *epespasato tēn machairan* combined with context = falling on it

## V.42 — "noble birth" vs. "noble birth" vs. "noble character"
- EMET/LOGOS: "noble birth" (Greek *eugeneia*)
- PNEUMA: "noble character" (substitutes character for birth/lineage)
- SOPHIA: "noble birth" — *eugeneia* specifically denotes lineage/birth, not merely character

## V.43 — "ran boldly up to the wall" vs. "ran up boldly to the wall" vs. "sprinted to the wall"
- EMET/LOGOS: retain "boldly"
- PNEUMA: "sprinted" (loses *tolmēros*: boldly/with daring)
- SOPHIA: EMET/LOGOS — "boldly" is theologically appropriate; it frames the act as courageous

## V.43 — "threw himself down bravely into the crowd" vs. "threw himself down bravely upon the crowd" vs. "threw himself off into the crowd below"
- EMET: "into the crowd"
- LOGOS: "upon the crowd"
- PNEUMA: "into the crowd below"
- SOPHIA: "threw himself down bravely into the crowd" — EMET

## V.45 — "blood gushing out in streams" vs. "blood streaming...in great gushes" vs. "blood pouring out in streams"
- Minor variation; all three agree on the image
- SOPHIA: "blood was gushing from his wounds in streams" — combined phrasing

## V.46 — "tore out his entrails" vs. "tore out his entrails" vs. "tore out his own entrails"
- All three agree; slight variation in possessive
- SOPHIA: "tore out his entrails" — no possessive needed

## V.46 — "calling upon the Lord of life and spirit" — all three agree exactly
- This title is unique in Greek literature; all three render it correctly
- SOPHIA: retain as "Lord of life and spirit" (*despotēn tēs zōēs kai tou pneumatos*)
